category_title: High-achieving dyslexic students using deep-level comprehension strategies
minimal_context: The student is reading an 891-word expository social studies text about socialization, norms, and sanctions to make notes on the most important information before a deadline.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read this 891-word text about socialization, norms, and sanctions by yourself and write down notes on the most important information before the deadline.

STUDENT: I am trying to read it, but I am getting slowed down by having to cope with the difficult words.

TUTOR: Just keep reading and do your best to take notes.

STUDENT: I want to make notes on the most important information, but working toward this deadline is making me stressed.

TUTOR: Try to finish reading the text by yourself.

STUDENT: I feel that I don’t learn very well from merely reading a text by myself. I think it works just fine to talk about the topics, to discuss them, but doing this alone is too slow.

options.A: Develop a class website for the social studies instruction, including a public discussion forum for sharing ideas and questions about socialization, norms, and sanctions.
options.B: Concentrate on the long-term teaching of a small repertoire of strategies typically used by good readers, for example predicting, questioning, imagining, clarifying, and summarizing.
options.C: Add a section to the opening of the class defining communication expectations, and to prevent students from taking over lectures, request that all questions be held until the end of class.
options.D: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the reading and note-taking tasks, requiring the student to finish the expository social studies text before the deadline.
